scenes.headline: How a 125B model decodes on one gaming GPU
scenes.sub: Strata, read from the source: one verify window, step by step.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Barfi! Let's open the engine that runs a giant mixture of experts on a gaming card.

scenes.text: Each layer rings a doorbell mid-graph, and every missed expert goes to the cache, the PCIe copy engine or the CPU at once.
scenes.say: Halfway through each layer, the GPU tells the processor which experts it needs, and three workers start together.

steps.say: The GPU runs attention and the router for every token in the window.
A tiny kernel writes the chosen expert ids into pinned memory, and the host sees them almost at once.
Cached experts run on the GPU. A share of the misses is copied over PCIe. The CPU computes the rest where they sit in RAM.
The next layer waits for the slowest lane, so the engine works to give them fewer experts.

scenes.title: How the cache follows the conversation
scenes.say: The VRAM cache learns which experts this chat keeps asking for.

items.say: Every routed expert adds one to a counter.
Every fourth round, pair the hottest missing experts with the coldest residents.
Swap only when the newcomer wins by a clear margin, and keep the biggest gains.
Then shrink every count, so old habits fade.

scenes.title: Where a window's time goes
scenes.text: t = dense + max(gpu, pcie, cpu) + draft

parts.note: always-used weights, read once per window
parts.say: First the GPU reads the always-used weights, once for the whole window.
Then the three lanes run together, and only the slowest one counts.
Last, the draft layer guesses the next few tokens.

steps.say: On one RTX thirty ninety, the drafts were accepted eighty-seven percent of the time.
A short prompt decoded at about ninety-six tokens a second, the long one at fifty-four.

scenes.label: VRAM hit rate the 3090 run implies
scenes.note: from the engine's own constants; not published
scenes.say: Rebuilt from the engine's constants, that speed needs most expert reads served from VRAM.

scenes.text: A bigger expert cache beats faster RAM: the slow lanes are PCIe and codebook arithmetic, not the DDR bus.
scenes.mark: A bigger expert cache beats faster RAM
scenes.say: So more VRAM beats faster RAM. That is why DDR4 and DDR5 measured almost the same.

recap: A doorbell hands experts to the CPU
scenes.say: A doorbell, three lanes, and a cache that learns.
